The *Nayamātikā* ("Matrix of Methods") is the opening section (Dt 1.1) of the *Dhātukathā*, the third book of the canonical Abhidhamma Piṭaka in the Theravāda tradition [SuttaCentral]. It functions as an introductory matrix or summary of the analytical methods (*naya*) governing the classifications in the remainder of the *Dhātukathā* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language [SuttaCentral]. The largest textual overlaps occur with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (11 matches; segments §4.1–15.1 aligning with §148_0–148_4) and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* (3 matches; segments §4.1–15.1 aligning with §69_0–69_4) [DharmaNexus]. Shared passages also appear within the Dhātukathā itself in the *Dutiyanaya Saṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadaniddesa* (Dt 2.2), as well as in the Abhidhamma sub-commentarial literature (*Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* and *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā*) and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus].
